analysis: Examined the Messages.swift changes visible in the supplied units. Head lines 248-251, 281-286 and 344-366 add an optional `busy: ProviderBusy?` field to ProviderMessage.Register and Heartbeat, with init plumbing. It is a provider-to-coordinator advisory signal (busy_reason, busy_since_ms, busy_addon) that marks a draining provider before its first heartbeat. It carries no prompt content, keys or credentials, and adds no bypass of attestation or App Attest authorization. The coordinator is trusted and treats provider-reported status as untrusted input anyway. The field is described as omitted when nil, and older coordinators ignore it. A malicious provider could already withhold work by reporting draining or by not serving, so there is no new capability. Base unit 5 (CoordinatorMessage decode/encode for load_model, prefetch, desired_models, trust_status and so on) appears unchanged in the supplied ranges; the changed base lines are 277, 354, 1328 and 1353. Not visible in the supplied units: the ProviderBusy type definition, its Codable encode/decode (the changed head ranges around 948-951, 1070, 1097 and 1345-1372), and the add-on hold producer. Those need checking in the same PR batch for bounded string lengths, no leakage of request-derived or sensitive text in busy_reason/busy_addon, and no log or telemetry exposure. Relevant threats: T-052 and T-053 are unaffected because busy is not authorization evidence. A-001 exposure is unlikely because the busy fields are metadata. No regressions identified in the supplied evidence, but the patch excerpt is truncated, so the encode/decode paths for busy were not seen.
